title: Ready to Rumble: Anthropic Rings the AI Bell
excerpt: Rumble signed a six-year, $13.7 billion AI hosting deal with Anthropic, shifting its business toward compute infrastructure and shares rose 11.6% as short se...
content_html:
Jeffrey Neal Johnson, MarketBeat

Tue, September 15, 2026 at 10:40 AM CDT 6 min read

Key Points

  • Interested in Rumble Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

  • Rumble signed a six-year, $13.7 billion hosting and compute deal with Anthropic, shifting its business toward enterprise AI infrastructure.

  • Shares of Rumble rose 11.6% on heavy volume while competitors CoreWeave and Nebius fell, as investors rotated capital toward the new contract.

  • Execution risks remain, including unfinanced construction costs for a 250MW Georgia facility and potential dilution from warrants tied to Anthropic's expansion.

When investors assess artificial intelligence infrastructure, established hyperscalers like Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN) or specialized operators like CoreWeave (NASDAQ: CRWV) usually dominate the discussion. However, one of the most intriguing transformations across the technology sector is actually emerging from an unexpected corner of digital media.

Rumble Inc. (NASDAQ: RUM) is executing a structural transition, shifting from an alternative video-sharing network into an enterprise compute supplier. Confirmation of a six-year, $13.7 billion hosting and compute agreement with AI research lab Anthropic has shifted Rumble's operational trajectory.

→ Could Dave & Buster's Capitulation Signal the Bottom Is Finally In?

This commercial agreement secures multi-year revenue visibility, decoupling Rumble's cash flows from cyclical digital advertising budgets and anchoring them to high-performance computing (HPC). For a business with trailing 12-month sales of about $100.62 million, a multi-billion-dollar backlog recalibrates valuation expectations. Physical infrastructure delivery creates real operational demands, but the arrangement shows how power-ready facilities can help bridge the current data center capacity shortage.

The $13.7B Heavyweight Deal

Under the contract, Rumble will supply Anthropic with dedicated AI hosting and computing infrastructure over six years. The agreement represents approximately $2.28 billion in contracted annual revenue. To put that figure in context, the total contract value stands at more than triple Rumble's market capitalization of about $3.8 billion in mid-September 2026.

→ Running on Empty: 3 Energy Plays for Europe's Deep Freeze

The announcement prompted immediate movement across the rented-compute ecosystem. Shares of competitors CoreWeave and Nebius Group (NASDAQ: NBIS) each dropped by roughly 5%-7% on Sept. 14 as details of the arrangement surfaced. Capital rotated toward Rumble, which closed up 11.6% at $8.58 per share, with trading volume topping 25 million shares, well above its 30-day average of about 3.93 million shares.
